why: getContextPath() joins caller-controlled id (and optionally projectId) with no resolve+containment check afterward. id='../../../../tmp/target' (with a real target file whose real name plus '.json' suffix exists, or reached via the paired write primitive below) escapes contextsDir/projectsDir entirely.

sink: fs.readdir(dir) then fs.readFile() on every '.json' file found -- no containment check after the join
why: When a projectId filter is supplied, it is joined into a directory path with no containment check, then every '.json' file in that arbitrary directory is read and its parsed content returned. projectId='../../../../etc' (or any directory containing readable .json files) discloses their content.

sink: fs.writeFile(contextPath, JSON.stringify(context), 'utf-8') -- no containment check after the join
why: Same unguarded getContextPath() join as get_context, used here for the write path. id='../../../../tmp/evil' (or any traversal target) writes caller-supplied JSON content to an arbitrary location the process can write to, with no existing-file precondition -- the most directly demonstrable of the four findings in this repo.
